metadata.title: Recursive Factorial
metadata.description: Compute factorial with a function that calls itself, with a correct base case.

instructions.main: Define a recursive `factorial(n)` — `factorial(0)` is `1` and `factorial(n)` is `n * factorial(n - 1)`.
steps: Otherwise `return n * factorial(n - 1)` — the function calls itself.

hints.message: Define `def factorial(n):` with a base case `if n <= 1: return 1` and `return n * factorial(n - 1)`.
This task requires recursion, not a loop — have `factorial` call itself: `return n * factorial(n - 1)`.
The base case must return `1`, not `0` — 0! is defined as 1, and returning 0 zeroes out every result.
Check the base case (`factorial(0)` must be 1) and make sure the recursive call is `factorial(n - 1)` so it reaches the base case.

evaluation.feedback_on_all_pass: `factorial` recurses to the base case and returns 120 for 5.

test_cases.feedback_on_fail: `factorial(5)` must return `120` — check the base case (`return 1`) and the recursive step (`n * factorial(n - 1)`).
Recursion means the function calls ITSELF — put `factorial(n - 1)` inside `factorial`, not a loop.
